title: Java foundations
description: A good foundation changes everything. Test your instincts on types, operators, strings, and the JVM.

questions.prompt: Which component executes Java bytecode?
questions.explanation: The Java Virtual Machine executes bytecode. javac compiles source into bytecode.

questions.prompt: What is the default value of an instance variable of type boolean?
questions.explanation: A boolean instance field defaults to false. Local variables must be initialized before use.

questions.prompt: Which keyword prevents a variable from being reassigned?
questions.explanation: A final variable can be assigned only once. A referenced object may still be mutable.

questions.prompt: What does System.out.println(5 / 2) print?
questions.explanation: Both operands are integers, so integer division discards the fractional part.

questions.prompt: Which method compares the contents of two strings?
questions.explanation: String.equals compares character content. == checks whether references point to the same object.

questions.prompt: Which is a valid Java entry point?
questions.explanation: The standard Java 17 entry point is public static void main(String[] args).

title: Think in objects
description: Go beyond syntax. Explore inheritance, polymorphism, encapsulation, and the choices behind good Java design.

questions.prompt: Which principle hides internal state behind a public interface?
questions.explanation: Encapsulation keeps implementation details and state behind a controlled interface.

questions.prompt: Which keyword calls a superclass constructor?
questions.explanation: super(...) invokes a constructor of the direct superclass.

questions.prompt: Method overriding is resolved primarily at which stage?
questions.explanation: For instance methods, runtime dispatch chooses the implementation based on the object's actual class.

questions.prompt: Can a Java class extend more than one class directly?
questions.explanation: Java classes have single class inheritance but may implement multiple interfaces.

questions.prompt: Which modifier prevents a class from being subclassed?
questions.explanation: A final class cannot be extended.

questions.prompt: An abstract class can contain which of these?
questions.explanation: Abstract classes can define state, constructors, concrete methods, and abstract methods.

title: Collections, decoded
description: Choose the right collection for the job. Lists, sets, maps, equality, and a few surprises along the way.

questions.prompt: Which collection guarantees unique elements?
questions.explanation: Set models a collection without duplicate elements according to its equality rules.

questions.prompt: Which Map preserves insertion order by default?
questions.explanation: LinkedHashMap maintains insertion order by default, or access order when explicitly configured.

questions.prompt: Average get-by-index time complexity for ArrayList is?
questions.explanation: ArrayList uses a backing array and supports constant-time indexed access.

questions.prompt: What must be consistent with equals() for hash collections?
questions.explanation: Equal objects must have the same hash code for hash-based collections to behave correctly.

questions.prompt: Which collection orders elements using natural ordering by default?
questions.explanation: TreeSet uses natural ordering unless a Comparator is supplied.

questions.prompt: Which queue operation returns null if the queue is empty?
questions.explanation: poll() returns null for an empty queue; remove() throws NoSuchElementException.

title: Handle the unexpected
description: Write resilient Java. Practice exception flow, resource management, and choosing the right recovery strategy.

questions.prompt: Which block is intended for cleanup after a try block?
questions.explanation: finally normally runs after try/catch, making it useful for cleanup. JVM termination can prevent it.

questions.prompt: Which is a checked exception?
questions.explanation: IOException is checked and must be caught or declared.

questions.prompt: Which interface enables try-with-resources?
questions.explanation: Resources in try-with-resources implement AutoCloseable so close() is called automatically.

questions.prompt: Which keyword explicitly raises an exception?
questions.explanation: throw raises an exception instance. throws declares exceptions in a method signature.

questions.prompt: What is the superclass of all exceptions and errors?
questions.explanation: Throwable is the common superclass of Exception and Error.

questions.prompt: How should multiple catch blocks be ordered?
questions.explanation: More specific exceptions must come before broader catches to avoid unreachable catch blocks.

title: Streams & lambdas
description: Find your flow with functional interfaces, stream pipelines, transformations, and lazy evaluation.

questions.prompt: Which stream operation is terminal?
questions.explanation: count() produces a result and terminates the stream pipeline.

questions.prompt: A functional interface has how many abstract methods?
questions.explanation: A functional interface has one abstract method, excluding qualifying Object methods. Default and static methods are allowed.

questions.prompt: Which operation transforms each stream element?
questions.explanation: map() transforms elements; filter() selects elements based on a predicate.

questions.prompt: What happens if you reuse a stream after a terminal operation?
questions.explanation: Streams are single-use. A detected reuse after consumption throws IllegalStateException.

questions.prompt: Which operation flattens nested streams?
questions.explanation: flatMap() maps each element to a stream and flattens the resulting streams.

questions.prompt: When are intermediate stream operations generally executed?
questions.explanation: Intermediate operations are lazy; terminal operations trigger processing.

title: Concurrency workshop
description: Threads, shared state, and execution. Put your understanding of concurrent Java to the test.

questions.prompt: Which method starts a new thread of execution?
questions.explanation: Thread.start() starts a new thread that calls run(). Calling run() directly stays on the current thread.

questions.prompt: What does synchronized primarily provide?
questions.explanation: Synchronized blocks provide mutual exclusion and establish memory visibility through monitor happens-before rules.

questions.prompt: Which class supports atomic integer increments?
questions.explanation: AtomicInteger supports operations like incrementAndGet() with atomic semantics.

questions.prompt: Which service manages pools of worker threads?
questions.explanation: ExecutorService manages task execution and lifecycle, often through a thread pool.

questions.prompt: Does volatile make count++ atomic?
questions.explanation: Volatile provides visibility and ordering. count++ is a read-modify-write operation and is not made atomic.

questions.prompt: What does Future.get() do before the result is ready?
questions.explanation: Future.get() waits for task completion and returns its result or throws an exception.
